docs.summary: Base class for effects in an [`AudioSource`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.AudioSource)'s processing chain.
docs.remarks: Parameters belong in serialized fields so the effect can be authored in the inspector and saved with the scene. Anything derived from the audio format belongs in [`OnInitialize`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Audio.Effects.AudioEffect~OnInitialize), which runs once the sample rate and channel count are known, rather than in a constructor that makes the caller pass in values the engine already has. [`OnProcess`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Audio.Effects.AudioEffect~OnProcess) runs on the audio thread. It must not allocate, block, or take a lock: a garbage collection or a contended lock there is an audible dropout, not a slow frame.

docs.summary: Passes audio through untouched while leaving the effect in the chain. Takes effect on the next block, from any thread.
docs.remarks: Tested per block rather than filtered out when the chain is built, so toggling this from gameplay works without anything having to republish the chain afterwards. The audio thread may read a value one block stale, which is inaudible, and the alternative was a toggle that only worked from the inspector.

docs.summary: Sample rate of the chain this effect is in. Valid from [`OnInitialize`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Audio.Effects.AudioEffect~OnInitialize) onward.
Channel count of the chain this effect is in. Valid from [`OnInitialize`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Audio.Effects.AudioEffect~OnInitialize) onward.
True once [`OnInitialize`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Audio.Effects.AudioEffect~OnInitialize) has run and the DSP state exists.

docs.summary: Binds the effect to an audio format and builds its DSP state. Safe to call more than once: it is what a source or bus calls when the effect joins it, and again whenever the format changes.
docs.remarks: Public so an effect can be driven outside a chain, for an offline render or a test of its own DSP. Until this runs there is no state for [`Process`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Audio.Effects.AudioEffect~Process) to work with, so an effect used that way does nothing at all.

docs.summary: Build DSP state sized to [`SampleRate`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Audio.Effects.AudioEffect~SampleRate) and [`Channels`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Audio.Effects.AudioEffect~Channels) here.
Pushes the current parameter values into the DSP state. Called after the inspector or a script edits the serialized fields directly, since those never go through the property setters.

docs.summary: Runs the effect over one block unless it is bypassed, and reports whether it did. Chains call this rather than [`OnProcess`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Audio.Effects.AudioEffect~OnProcess), so bypassing is honoured the same way everywhere.

docs.summary: Processes one block on the audio thread. Leaving `framesOut` untouched passes the previous stage's output through unchanged.
Called when the effect is removed from its source, or the source is destroyed.
